title: 20-22. THE PRIESTS' LAND WAS NOT BOUGHT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Joseph bought all the land in Egypt for Pharaoh. The Egyptians, one and all, sold their fields, because the famine was too severe for them. The land became Pharaoh's, and Joseph reduced the people to servitude, from one end of Egypt to the other. However, he did not buy the land of the priests, because they received a regular allotment from Pharaoh and had food enough from the allotment Pharaoh gave them. That is why they did not sell their land." — Gen 47:20-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Everyone in Egypt loses their land except one group: the priests. Because they were on a state allowance, they never had to sell.

The text mentions this without comment. But it quietly shows us how life works. Some people are sheltered from a crisis by a position they happened to hold. It was not that the priests were more deserving, or wiser, or more faithful. They simply had a different arrangement.

This is worth naming, because we are prone to two errors. When we are the ones spared, we assume it says something good about us. When we are the ones who lose everything, we assume it says something bad about us. Neither is reliable.

Jesus corrected exactly this thinking. When people asked about a tower that collapsed and killed eighteen, He said plainly they were not worse sinners than anyone else (Lk 13:4-5). Job's friends built entire speeches on the assumption that suffering proves guilt, and God told them they had spoken wrongly.

If you have been spared something, be grateful and humble. If you have lost much, do not read God's opinion of you in your circumstances. Read it at the cross.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you read God's approval or disapproval into your circumstances?
2. If you have been spared hardship, how does that shape how you treat others?
3. Where do you actually see God's love for you most clearly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from measuring Your love by my circumstances. Make me humble when I am spared and steady when I am not, and let the cross be where I read Your heart towards me. Amen.
